cells: PLANNING PROMPTS  |  Additions from JIS IA Guide (2025)
Use these short questions after the corresponding flowchart nodes. They should not form one compulsory questionnaire.
Optional idea comparison, predictions, future changes and teacher questions accept 'Not sure yet' or Skip.

Comparisons, predictions and planned adjustments are optional; milestone dates are editable, and unknown school deadlines remain 'To confirm with teacher'. The guide's planning-to-draft-to-revision sequence is reflected here.
Teacher discussions are recommended for everyone and required before pursuing certain flagged ideas/actions, never before exporting a summary.
Every recorded answer can appear in the student's personalised planning report; only relevant sections are displayed.
What other IA topic could you investigate? (Up to two additional ideas.)
One idea is fine; this branch must be skippable.
Which idea offers the easiest access to suitable data, and why?
Use quick comparison; no need for complete second plan.
Which idea is most useful/interesting and realistic given your time?
Do not rank popularity as mathematical quality.
Which idea would you like to plan now?
Keep alternatives recorded without treating them as failed ideas.
After course and initial maths choices (N04S); IA type and relevant data context known
What sort of result or pattern do you think you might find? Pick a relevant suggestion, enter your own prediction or choose 'Not sure yet'.
Context-filtered prediction choice(s), Other text or Not sure
Prediction nudge depends on IA type and data context. After it, ask separately WHY, and what it might mean for the selected beneficiary IF TRUE (P06); allow edit at N01V before maths review.
Whenever the student makes a prediction
WHY do you expect this? What experience, observation or reasoning supports your prediction?
Separate short-answer box (optional if genuinely unsure)
Keep WHY distinct from the implication question (P06). Neither is a fabricated result. If unsure, accept uncertainty and proceed.
Every student after defining an investigation aim
Who could benefit from knowing the answer to your investigation?
Choose one: It would help me / I could advise someone / Both / Not sure yet
Continue to one or two short conditional questions. Personal usefulness counts; do not require a grand real-world impact.
What other realistic method of collecting or finding this data did you consider?
For Both, wait until both source branches are answered.
Why is your selected method preferable for this investigation?
Explain fit to aim, not generic pros and cons.
What is the main limitation of your chosen collection/source method?
Different prompts for surveys, measurements and secondary sources.
Can you reduce this limitation, or why is it acceptable?
Accept honest limitations without pretending to eliminate them.
What population and sampling method will you use? What alternative was possible?
Check bias and survey wording; reuse data already entered.
What initial-idea, teacher-draft and final deadlines has your school set?
No invented dates; 'To confirm with teacher' is valid.
Data or simplified example will be used
By what date could you prepare an initial graph, diagram or simplified case?
Must fit the expected data availability where applicable.
When could you complete an initial calculation and reflect on it?
Encourage an early start, not a late all-at-once calculation.
When will your written first draft, including analysis and conclusion, be ready?
Use the school's teacher-draft deadline where available.
When will you check, correct and submit your revised IA?
Reserve time for self-check and teacher feedback.
What could you start earlier or simplify to create a buffer?
Flag clashes with known deadlines; don't block summary export.
What simple graph, table, diagram or simplified version of the problem might help you begin?
Plan only; don't require students to produce the actual graph yet.
What might it help you notice, compare or calculate?
Link the representation back to the investigation aim.
What result or difficulty might cause you to change the direction of your investigation?
Recognise that plans evolve; unsuccessful results are worth reflecting on.
What could you modify without restarting your whole IA?
E.g. refine variables, model or sample; avoid committing to a fixed structure.
Is there anything about your aim or plan you would like to discuss with your teacher?
Use N08 teacher answers if previously supplied; do not ask twice.
If student wants to book check-in
When could you discuss your plan with your teacher?
Conversation recommended, not required before export.
When will your initial planning and introductory explanation be ready?
Pre-fill teacher-provided dates when known, never invent them.
When will you analyse and reflect on your initial graph, table or simplified case?
A graph alone is not enough; leave time to interpret it.
When multiple mathematical steps are planned
When will you complete further calculations, analyse the results and write your conclusion?
Plan for reflection before the teacher's draft deadline.
What initial graph or data sample might help you work out what to expect?
Accept uncertainty; don't block the next maths-review node.
How to explore an uncertain prediction
Look again at your earlier maths choices. Would you keep, add or remove any techniques?
Existing multi-select reopened; optional Other; Not sure
Show course-specific suggestions based on chosen prediction. No forced additions.
When a suggested technique is displayed
Why might this mathematics help investigate the pattern you expect?
Use explanation to assess fit; don't demand an essay or pretend suggestion is essential.
Does the method fit your variables and expected pattern?
Short contextual note with edit controls
E.g. PMCC requires paired numerical data and concerns linear association; a normal distribution describes one numerical variable, not correlation.
Would you like to record another technique not on your course list?
Retain any existing free-text choice; suggest teacher consultation, not automatic rejection.
Only when data structure cannot be inferred from prior answers
Which best describes your data: two numerical quantities, one numerical variable, comparing groups, categorical variables, repeated yes/no trials, or something else?
Use only to filter sensible prediction nudges. Do not repeat data-type questions if variables already make this clear.
If personal benefit or Both is chosen
What might you decide, do, improve or understand better after answering your question? Why would that be useful to you?
Prompt a realistic, directly useful outcome rather than simply naming a mathematical technique. Findings need not confirm the prediction.
If advice to someone or Both is chosen
Who might find your results useful (person, role or group), and what decision or advice might your findings help them with? Why would that matter?
A teacher, team, school group, family member or other realistic audience is fine. Don't request identifiable third-party details. Advice must ultimately follow evidence.
After a prediction is selected and WHY has been answered, if an intended beneficiary is known
Your aim: [student's current aim]. If [selected prediction] were true, what would it mean for [current beneficiary]? How could this help answer your aim or inform a decision or advice?
Separate short-answer box or 'Not sure yet'

Display aim and prediction above the answer box. Address the selected beneficiary naturally ('you' for self, 'your friend / group' for others). Allow Not sure yet; keep it hypothetical. Show 'Edit who is this for?' beside the prompt.
Inline Edit link opening N01V fields; Confirm/Back to prediction

Reopen the original beneficiary and intended-use fields in place, then return directly to prediction. Retain draft implication; if beneficiary changes, ask to confirm/edit it rather than silently discard.

SOURCE: JIS SL Maths IA Guide 2025 — https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1BesCf9vTKGLm588jx5SUIdLyz-x5HUyYb2LqG_BACKg/edit
